import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_transport_crime.csv')
adjacency = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Create spatial weights matrix
boroughs = df['borough'].values
n = len(boroughs)
W = np.zeros((n, n))

# Map borough names to indices
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Fill weights matrix
for _, row in adjacency.iterrows():
    if row['borough'] in borough_to_idx and row['neighbor'] in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
        j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
        W[i, j] = 1
        W[j, i] = 1  # symmetric adjacency

# Standardize weights matrix row-wise
W = W / W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
W = np.nan_to_num(W)  # handle boroughs with no neighbors

# Calculate Lee's L statistic
X = df['Transport_value'].values
Y = df['Crime_value'].values()

X_std = (X - X.mean()) / X.std()
Y_std = (Y - Y.mean()) / Y.std()

n = len(X)
S0 = W.sum()
Lee_L = (X_std @ W @ Y_std) / S0

print("Lee's L:", Lee_L)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_transport_crime.csv')
adjacency = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Create complete borough list and verify adjacency coverage
all_boroughs = set(df['borough'])
adjacent_boroughs = set(adjacency['borough']).union(set(adjacency['neighbor']))
missing_in_adjacency = all_boroughs - adjacent_boroughs
print(f"Boroughs missing from adjacency data: {missing_in_adjacency}")

# Create spatial weights matrix with guaranteed connectivity
boroughs = df['borough'].values
n = len(boroughs)
W = np.zeros((n, n))

# Create borough to index mapping
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build adjacency matrix with fallback to k-nearest neighbors if needed
for _, row in adjacency.iterrows():
    if row['borough'] in borough_to_idx and row['neighbor'] in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
        j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
        W[i, j] = 1
        W[j, i] = 1  # Ensure symmetry

# For completely isolated boroughs, connect to nearest 3 boroughs by Transport_value
coords = df[['Transport_value']].values
for i in range(n):
    if W[i].sum() == 0:  # Isolated borough
        distances = np.abs(coords - coords[i])
        nearest = np.argsort(distances.flatten())[1:4]  # Skip self, take next 3
        for j in nearest:
            W[i, j] = 1
            W[j, i] = 1

# Row-standardize the weights matrix
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
W = W / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

# Calculate Lee's L with validation
X = df['Transport_value'].values
Y = df['Crime_value'].values

# Standardize variables
X_std = (X - X.mean()) / X.std()
Y_std = (Y - Y.mean()) / Y.std()

# Compute spatial correlation with validation
S0 = W.sum()
if S0 > 0:
    Lee_L = (X_std @ W @ Y_std) / S0
else:
    Lee_L = np.nan

# Permutation test with validation
if not np.isnan(Lee_L):
    n_permutations = 500
    count_extreme = 0
    for _ in range(n_permutations):
        Y_perm = np.random.permutation(Y)
        Y_perm_std = (Y_perm - Y_perm.mean()) / Y_perm.std()
        perm_L = (X_std @ W @ Y_perm_std) / S0
        if perm_L >= Lee_L:  # One-tailed test
            count_extreme += 1
    p_value = count_extreme / n_permutations
else:
    p_value = np.nan

print("Final Lee's L:", Lee_L)
print("Final p-value:", p_value)
